game_theory.description: Market participants face a coordination game where fund flows and option convexity create positive feedback loops: expectations of higher copper prices drive call buying, which amplifies price moves, attracting further momentum traders. Leader-follower dynamics emerge as commodity leaders like FMLI draw inflows, while laggards suffer from reduced liquidity. Sanctions and geopolitical risk introduce a strategic layer where policymakers' actions (e.g., gasoline price hikes) affect market sentiment and option pricing.
uncertainty: Lack of real-time option Greeks prevents precise equilibrium calculation

dynamic_system.description: A dynamic feedback loop links copper price → realized sales price/margins → FMLI earnings expectations → fund flow rotation → price/volume confirmation → option convexity → further price pressure. Volume-quality feedback reinforces the loop when sales growth is volume-led. Disruptions (copper price breakdown, volume decay) act as negative feedback or regime shift triggers.
uncertainty: Missing real-time price and volume data prevents precise calibration of loop gains
